Odoo is an open-source ERP platform that integrates various business applications like CRM, Sales, Inventory, HR, and more into a single system. <!-- image --> ## Odoo Editions - Community Edition : Free, open-source version. - Enterprise Edition : Paid version with extra features and support. ## Odoo Structure - Backend : Python, PostgreSQL, XML - Frontend : QWeb (HTML/XML), JavaScript - ORM : Object-Relational Mapping to manage the database using Python classes. ## Installing Odoo on Ubuntu Step 1 : System Update : sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y ## Step 2 : Install Required Packages sudo apt install git python3-pip build-essential wget python3-dev python3-venv python3-wheel libxslt-dev libzip-dev libldap2-dev libsasl2-dev python3-setuptools node-less libjpeg-dev libpq-dev gcc g++ -y ## Step 3 : PostgreSQL Installation - -sudo apt install postgresql -y - -sudo -u postgres createuser --createdb --username postgres --no-createrole --no-superuser odoo15 ## Step 4 : Install Wkhtmltopdf - -sudo apt install xfonts-75dpi xfonts-base -y - -wget https ://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/packaging/releases/download/0.12.6-1/wkhtmltox\_0.12.6-1.bionic\_ amd 64.deb - -sudo apt install ./wkhtmltox\_0.12.6-1.bionic\_amd64.deb ## Step 5 : Download Odoo Source Code - -git clone https ://github.com/odoo/odoo --depth 1 --branch 15.0 --single-branch odoo15 - -cd odoo15 ## Step 6 : Create Python Virtual Environment - -python3 -m venv odoo-venv - -source odoo-venv/bin/activate - -pip3 install wheel - -pip3 install -r requirements.txt ## Step 7 : Run Odoo Server ./odoo-bin -d odoo15 -i base --addons-path=addons --db-filter=odoo15 ## Lab 3 : Odoo Basics ## Understanding Odoo Components - Models : Define database structure using Python classes. - Views : Define the user interface (form, list, kanban). - Menus : Add navigational menus. - Security : Manage access rights using ACL and record rules. ## Practical Example : Student Model ## Model Definition ``` name = fields.Char(string='Student Name', required=True) ``` ``` from odoo import models, fields class Student(models.Model) : _name = 'student.student' _description = 'Student' age = fields.Integer(string='Age') student_class = fields.Char(string='Class') ``` ## Views Definition ``` <record id="view_student_form" model="ir.ui.view"> ``` ``` <field name="name">student.form</field> <field name="model">student.student</field> <field name="arch" type="xml"> <form string="Student"> <sheet> <group> <field name="name"/> <field name="age"/> <field name="student_class"/> </group> ``` ``` </sheet> </form> </field> </record> <record id="view_student_tree" model="ir.ui.view"> <field name="name">student.tree</field> <field name="model">student.student</field> <field name="arch" type="xml"> <tree string="Students"> <field name="name"/> <field name="age"/> <field name="student_class"/> </tree> </field> </record> ``` ## Menu Items ``` <menuitem id="menu_student_root" name="Student Management"/> <menuitem id="menu_student" name="Students" parent="menu_student_root" action="action_student"/> ``` ## Security ## Create ir.model.access.csv id,name,model\_id :id,group\_id :id,perm\_read,perm\_write,perm\_create,perm\_unlink ``` access_student,access.student,model_student_student,base.group_user,1,1,1,1 ``` ## Explanation of ir.model.access.csv ## 1. File Purpose : Defines which user groups can access which models and what actions (CRUD) they are allowed to perform. ## 2. CSV Columns : - id : Unique technical ID for the access rule. - name : Display name of the access rule. - model\_id :id : The model this rule applies to (example : student.student model). - group\_id :id : The user group this rule is for (example : base.group\_user means Employees). - perm\_read : 1 = can read records, 0 = cannot. - perm\_write : 1 = can edit records, 0 = cannot. -

Our Example Line : access\_student,access.student,model\_student\_student,base.group\_user,1,1,1,1 ## 4. Meaning : - ID : access\_student (unique internal ID) - Name : access.student (display name) - Model : student.student (applies to Student model) - Group : base.group\_user (applies to Employees) - Permissions : - ■ Read : Yes - ■ Write : Yes - ■ Create : Yes - ■ Delete : Yes ## 5. Effect : Employees can fully manage (read, create, update, delete) all student records. ## 6. Example of Read-Only Rule : access\_student,access.student,model\_student\_student,base.group\_user,1,0,0,0 👉 This means employees can only read student records, no create, edit, or delete allowed. ## Lab 4 : Advanced Development ## Relationships - Many2one : One student belongs to one class. - One2many : One class has many students. - Many2many : Many students can enroll in many subjects. ## Example : Many2one ``` class ClassRoom(models.Model) : _name = 'student.class' name = fields.Char(string='Class Name') class Student(models.Model) : _name = 'student.student' name = fields.Char(string='Student Name') ``` ``` class_id = fields.Many2one('student.class', string='Class') ``` ## Computed Fields A computed field is a field whose value is automatically calculated by Odoo , based on other fields or logic you define. ## Key Features: - The value is not stored manually. - It can be stored or dynamic : - store=True → Odoo saves it in the database (can be searched/sorted). - store=False (default) → Computed at display time only. - Requires a compute method decorated with @api.depends. ``` from odoo import api @api.depends('subject_ids.grade') def _compute_average_grade(self) : for record in self : grades = [subject.grade for subject in record.subject_ids] record.average_grade = sum(grades) / len(grades) if grades else 0 ``` ## Scheduled Actions - A Scheduled Action (cron job) in Odoo is a task that automatically executes at specified time intervals (e.g., every day, every hour). - Useful for background processes like : - Sending automatic reminders. - Cleaning up old data. - Generating reports. ## Key Features : - Runs automatically based on a cron schedule . - Can execute Python methods from your models. - Configured from Settings > Technical > Automation > Scheduled Actions. - Defined in Python code and optionally registered via XML. ## 1. XML Configuration <odoo> <record id="ir_cron_student_report" model="ir.cron"> <field name="name">Daily Student Report</field> <field name="model_id" ref="model_student_student"/> <field name="state">code</field> <field name="code">model.send_daily_student_report()</field> <field name="interval_number">1</field> <field name="interval_type">days</field> <field name="numbercall">-1</field> <!-- -1 means unlimited calls --> <field name="active">True</field> </record> </odoo> -name : The title of the scheduled action (for identification). -model_id : The model where the Python method is located. -state : Must always be "code" for Python execution. -code : Python instruction to run (example: model.send_daily_student_report()). -interval_number : The frequency number (like 1). -interval_type : Time unit (minutes, hours, days, weeks, months). -numbercall : Number of allowed executions: ● -1 → unlimited ● 1 → execute only once ``` - -active : Whether the scheduled action is enabled (True) or not. ## Types of Intervals - interval\_type = 'minutes' → every X minutes. - interval\_type = 'hours' → every X hours. - interval\_type = 'days' → every X days. ## How to View and Edit in Odoo 1. Go to Settings > Technical > Automation > Scheduled Actions . 2. Search for your scheduled job. 3. You can change the frequency, enable/disable it, or run it manually. ## Notes: - Scheduled actions are managed by the Odoo worker process . - If using a multi-worker production setup, make sure workers are configured to handle cron jobs. - The ir.cron records can be created via XML or manually from the Odoo UI. ## Lab 5 : Odoo API Integration ## Connect to Odoo via XML-RPC ``` import xmlrpc.client url = 'http ://localhost :8069' db = 'odoo15' username = 'admin' password = 'admin' common = xmlrpc.client.ServerProxy(f'{url}/xmlrpc/2/common') uid = common.authenticate(db, username, password, {}) models = xmlrpc.client.ServerProxy(f'{url}/xmlrpc/2/object') ``` # Create a student models.execute\_kw(db, uid, password, 'student.student', 'create', [{'name' : 'Ali', 'age' : 18}]) ## Lab 6 : Building REST API in Odoo ## Odoo Controller ``` from odoo import http from odoo.http import request class StudentAPI(http.Controller) : @http.route('/api/students', auth='public', type='json', methods=['GET']) def get_students(self) : students = request.env['student.student'].sudo().search([]) return [{'id' : s.id, 'name' : s.name, 'age' : s.age} for s in students] ``` ## Lab 7 : Mobile App Integration - Use React Native / Flutter to fetch data from /api/students. - Use Axios to perform GET requests to Odoo. ## Example React Native Code ``` axios.get('http ://localhost :8069/api/students') .then(response => console.log(response.data)) .catch(error => console.error(error)); ``` ## Lab 8 : Deployment & Security

PROCUREMENT & PURCHASE APPROVAL POLICY Document Version: 1.0 Effective Date: 01 January 2025 Applicable System: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) System Department Owner: Finance & Procurement ## 1. Purpose This document defines the procurement and purchase approval process followed within the ERP system of mpinext Manufacturing Pvt. Ltd. The objective of this policy is to ensure controlled purchasing, financial accountability, and compliance with internal audit requirements. All procurement activities must be initiated, approved, and recorded through the ERP system. ## 2. Scope This policy applies to all employees involved in procurement-related activities, including: - Purchase requisition creation - Purchase approval and authorization - Purchase order generation - Invoice verification and payment processing Manual purchases or offline approvals outside the ERP system are strictly prohibited unless explicitly approved as an exception. ## 3. Roles and Responsibilities Role Responsibilities and ERP Permissions Employee Create purchase requisitions in the ERP system Department Manager Approve purchase requisitions up to ₹50,000 Finance Manager Approve purchase requisitions above ₹50,000 Procurement Officer Convert approved requisitions into Purchase Orders Accounts Team Verify invoices and process payments Each role is assigned system permissions within the ERP to ensure segregation of duties. ## 4. Purchase Requisition and Approval Workflow The procurement workflow within the ERP system follows these steps: 1. An employee raises a Purchase Requisition in the ERP system with required details such as item description, quantity, and justification. 2. The requisition is automatically routed to the respective Department Manager for approval. 3. If the requisition value exceeds ₹50,000, it is forwarded to the Finance Manager for additional approval. 4. Upon approval, the Procurement Officer generates a Purchase Order (PO) in the ERP system. 5. The Purchase Order is issued to the selected vendor through the ERP system. No purchase shall be made without an approved Purchase Order. ## 5. Invoice Processing and Payment Invoice processing is handled through the ERP system as follows: 1. Vendors submit invoices referencing the corresponding Purchase Order number. 2. The Accounts Team performs a three-way match between: 3. o Purchase Order 4. o Goods Receipt Note 5. o Vendor Invoice 3. Any discrepancies are flagged in the ERP system for review. 4. Once verified, invoices are approved for payment and scheduled as per payment terms. Invoices without valid Purchase Orders will not be processed. ## 6. Escalation Rules The ERP system enforces the following escalation rules: - Purchase requisitions pending approval for more than 3 working days are automatically escalated to the next approval authority. - Rejected requisitions must include a rejection reason in the ERP system. - Emergency or urgent purchases require Finance Manager approval irrespective of purchase value. ## 7. Compliance and Audit All procurement transactions are logged within the ERP system and are subject to internal and external audits. - Audit logs must be retained for a minimum period of 5 years . - Any deviation from this policy will be treated as a compliance violation. - Procurement activities conducted outside the ERP system may result

Each time you add a table or file to a project you import metadata, which the software stores in your repository. If you and your coworkers add the same table or file to multiple projects, there are multiple instances of the same metadata. SAP Information Steward manages this metadata by storing only one copy of the metadata in the repository. Therefore, all projects that have the same table or file, share the same copy of the imported table or file metadata. Because metadata is shared between multiple projects, make sure that you understand the following conditions about shared tables and files: - If the schema changes in the external source, and you reimport the metadata into one project, all instances of the metadata in projects that share the metadata update to reflect the changes. - You can't delete table or file metadata when other projects are still using the metadata. ## Changes to external tables Imported metadata doesn't change when the external table changes. For example, when a column name changes or a column is deleted in a table, which changes the schema, the column name in Data Insight doesn't change nor does the metadata reflect the deleted column. Because external changes aren't automatically updated in imported metadata, you must reconcile metadata in the project. Before you reconcile imported metadata, delete any objects associated with the changed metadata in the external source. For example, if a column is deleted, make sure that you delete any rule bindings or tasks associated with the column in all related projects before you reconcile the table metadata. The Set Optimal Order dialog displays the number of rows in a table to assist you. ##  Note Data Insight gets the number of rows when you run column profiling on the table. Otherwise, the number of rows is blank. 3. Select a caching type from the Cache list for each join. 4. When you are finished, select OK . The software processes your joins based on the ranking that you set. The software processes the highest ranking table first, the second highest rank second, and so on. The desired result is faster processing. Views that contain SAP tables have the potential to be quite large, especially when they are joined with other SAP tables. The limit of 500 records when viewing data prevents your computer from hanging or never completing the task because the tables were too large. In addition to the 500 records limit, you can take steps to enhance performance in the following ways: - Reduce the size of the file by mapping fields, join conditions, filters, and so on to limit the data in the table to information that you really need. - Use SAP ABAP-supported functions in forming expressions in views. Using non-supported functions is allowed, but doing so may adversely affect performance. - Use the View Data filter tools when you view and export data from SAP tables. With the 500 records limit for viewing SAP table data, there is a potential for no records showing up in the View Data window. This could happen, for example, when the view contains a child view, the child view contains one or more SAP tables, and a join is set up to join the entire data set. A message appears at the top of the View Data window that instructs you to export the data to an external source (text file, CSV, or Excel file) to view all of the records. Content types add an additional dimension to your data by providing meaning. Content types categorize your data based on data type and the content of the column. Data Insight provides predefined content types, such as name, firm, phone, date, and address. You can create custom content types that Data Insight includes in suggestions from a content type profile. You can accept the suggested content type or enter your own content type based on the profile results. ##  Example A column named Contact\_Info includes data such as e-mail, phone, or address. After a content type profile, look at the profiling results for the number and percent of records that appear to be e-mail, phone, or address data. Use the number and percent data to decide to accept or reject the suggested content type. Content Type profiling uses custom logic such as proximity to other fields, patterns, and so on, to provide a content type that gives meaning to your data. Content types are useful when defining rules and having rules automatically suggested after profiling. ##  Note Columns with BLOB, CLOB, and Long data types can't be assigned a content type. Data Insight becomes better at assigning your custom content types, and learns to correlate other data with similar characteristics with the custom content type. ##  Restriction Before Data Insight automatically suggests the custom content types for other tables, run a column profiling task with the Median & Distribution option selected. Otherwise, Data Insight doesn't autoassociate columns to this content type for other tables. After you accept the suggested custom content type for one table, Data Insight 'learns' to associate the data type to the content type. ##  Example You created a content type named Reward Number and assigned it to a column that has numeric data in the format 9-777-51912. Then you run a content type profile task on a table that has a numeric column with the n-nnn-nnnnn pattern. This anomaly happens because of internal minimum thresholds. Minimum threshold requirements for predefined content types are higher than for custom content types. Rule tasks fail on subsequent runs when you select the option Append failed data when you configure the failed data connection in the Central Management Console (CMC) and either of the following occurs: - You make a structural change to your source data. - You change the is\_unique or is\_data\_dependent in the rule binding. Under these circumstances, Data Insight can't add data to the failed data repository because the structure doesn't match the current data structure from previous runs of the rule task. The following structural changes to source data made between executions of a rule task causes the rule tasks to fail on subsequent executions: - Add a new column or remove an existing column. - Add or remove a primary key designation. - Change a primary key designation from one column to a different column. ## Rerun rule task successfully Data Insight offers two options to automatically delete related objects in the failed data repository and rerun the rule tasks: - In the Tasks tab of Data Insight, select the failed rule task and click the Delete Failed Data and Run icon at the top of the page. Data Insight deletes the related objects from the failed data repository. Then select to rerun the rule task. - In the Data Insight Project node in the CMC, right-click the failed rule task and select Delete Failed Data and Run from the dropdown menu. Data Insight deletes related objects in the failed data repository. Then select to rerun the rule task. ##  Note The Delete Failed Data and Run option is available only when the rule task fails because of data structure inconsistencies. If the option isn't available, examine the rule task log file for information about why the rule task failed. When you change a setting in a rule task and save the rule task, Data Insight creates additional metadata tables based on the rule task change. <!-- image --> ##  Example With the option Include Source selected, you run the order\_amount\_rule rule task. The rule task creates the failed data metadata table named ORDER\_AMOUNT\_RULE\_FD , which contains one row for each record that failed the rule task. However, when you edit the rule task and deselect Include Source , and rerun the order\_amount\_rule rule task, the rule task fails. The rule task fails because, when you change the rule task option, Data Insight tries to re-create the ORDER\_AMOUNT\_RULE\_FD metadata table, but discovers that the failed data repository already has that object, so it fails the rule task. When the rule task fails because of a pre-existing object, Data Insight offers to automatically delete the related objects in the failed data repository so you can rerun the rule task successfully. The options are available when you right-click the rule task in the following dialogs: - Select the name of the rule task in the Tasks tab of Data Insight and click the Delete Failed Data and Run icon at the top of the page. - Right-click the name of the rule task in the Central Management Console under Data Insight Projects node and select Delete Failed Data and Run . ##  Note The Delete Failed Data and Run option is active only when the rule task fails because of data structure inconsistencies such as a pre-existing object. If the Delete Failed Data and Run option isn't active and the status is showing that the rule task failed, it may not have failed because of a structural change in the repository. In this case, look at the log file for information about why the rule task failed. The comments state that 'One or more rule bindings already exist and overwrite is not enabled.' ## 3.11 Data Cleansing Advisor Data Cleansing Advisor simplifies the data cleansing process by intelligently recommending a data cleansing solution for your data. Data Cleansing Advisor bases the recommendations on content-type profiling results and SAP best practices for your specific data. A complete data cleansing solution is a collection of cleansing and matching rules for party data in your source. Party data is data about individuals or organizations, such as customer data and vendor data. Examples of party data include name, address, and phone data. Through the Data Cleansing Advisor wizard, you develop a cleansing solution. Before you publish the solution, see how the data cleansing solution affects your data by viewing cleanse and match results on sample data. If the data preview reveals unsatisfactory results, change option settings and view the revised results. Data Cleansing Advisor creates staged data using the source data, and works only on the staged data. Therefore, the results that you view in the wizard are temporary and for planning purposes only. The wizard doesn't change the original source data until you publish the Data Cleansing Soution and use it in SAP Data Services Workbench. For more information about using an SAP Information Steward Data Cleansing Solution in the Workbench, see the Workbench Guide. ##  Note You must have a compatible version of either Information platform services (IPS) or SAP BusinessObjects Business Intelligence (BI) platform and SAP Data Services for successful data cleansing solutions. Data Cleansing Advisor performs matching based on the match theme and match rules that you select in the Data Cleansing Advisor wizard. In some cases, Data Cleansing Advisor uses multiple match rules that fall under the main match rule that you selected in the wizard. <!-- image --> ##  Example If you select the match rule Person and Address in the wizard, Data Cleansing Advisor uses multiple Person and Address match rules, each one designed for a specific type of address, to search for matching records. The Match Rule column, which you can view in Match Results data view and also in the Record Comparison Viewer , shows the specific match rule that Data Cleansing Advisor used to consider the record pair to be matching records. Data Cleansing Advisor applies the match rules that you select in a specific order as the following example shows. ##  Example You select the Person and ID match rule and the Person and Phone match rule. Data Cleansing Advisor applies match rules in the following order: 1. ID: Either ID only, or something and ID, such as Person and ID. 2. Phone: Either Phone only, or something and Phone, such as Person and Phone. 3. E-mail: Either e-mail only, or something and e-mail, such as Person and e-mail. 4. Date: Either Date only, or something and Date, such as Person and Date. 5. Address:

Select OK to close the Manage Email Notifications dialog box. ## 3.12.3 How scorecards are calculated Data Insight calculates a scorecard using scores from all objects in the key data domain. The formula for calculating the scorecard is fairly straightforward: - The rule bindings for a rule are calculated and combined to equal the score for the rule. - The scores for the rules are combined to equal the score for the quality dimension. - The scores for the quality dimensions are combined to equal the key data domain (KDD) score. The weight for each object group must total 100%. ##  Note If you assign a weight of zero to an item, the item (including its children) doesn't appear and isn't used in any calculations in the scorecard view. Information Steward calculates the scorecard score and saves it in the local repository using the Calculate Scorecard utility. Administrators schedule the Calculate Scorecard utility in the Central Management Console (CMC). By default, the Calculate Scorecard utility runs daily, but your administrator can change the frequency in the CMC. Also, a rule task calculates the scores for rule bindings. Rule tasks calculate the scores for all rules bound to tables, flat files, and views. ## Example A KDD named Customer has the following quality dimensions: - Accuracy - Completeness - Conformity The Conformity quality dimension has two rules: - Validate Postal Code - Validate Phone Number The rule Validate Phone Number has two rule bindings: - TableA.phone - TableB.contact.info The following diagram shows the components in the scorecard. When specifying a decimal data type in Information Steward, you indicate the following characteristics of the type: <precision> : The total number of digits in the value. <scale> : The number of digits to the right of the decimal point. In the software, the following relations must hold for <precision> and <scale> : ``` 1 <= precision <= 28 (Oracle datastore: 1<= precision <= 96 ) ``` ``` 0 <= scale <= precision ``` The decimal value can have a plus or minus sign indicating a positive or negative value. The sign can appear before or after the value with any number of blanks between the value and the sign. Unsigned values are considered to be nonnegative. The sign does not count as part of <precision> . Leading zeros are permitted in the integer digit, and trailing zeros are permitted in the fraction part. Input that is more precise than the data type of the column or variable in which it is stored is rounded. Input out of range (absolute value is too large) causes a runtime error. This data type allows NULL values. The decimal data type and the numeric data type are identical in the software. When specifying a varchar data type, indicate the following characteristic of the type: <length> Number of characters that the variable or column can hold. <Length> must be greater than zero. There is no maximum allowable value for the <length> . Character strings longer than the number of characters defined for the column or variable are truncated on the right to the length of the data type. Only the required number of characters is used to store strings shorter than <length> . Information Steward provides functions to convert values to and from strings; to join strings together, use the concatenation operator ( || ). This data type allows NULL values. The software conforms to the ANSI SQL-92 varchar standard and treats varchar data as follows: - Keeps trailing blanks in character values that you insert into varchar columns. - Keeps trailing blanks when you read from sources with string data types. If you want to remove trailing blanks from your input data, you must use the Right trim function. ##  Note If the original data type is char, the software does not trim the trailing blanks. - Ignores trailing blanks when you compare varchar data in functions (Decode, Lookup Value). ##  Note Not all database servers follow the ANSI standard for trailing blanks in insert, select, and compare operations. Therefore, if the software pushes down the insert, select, and compare operations to the database servers, the operations might return different results than when the software evaluates them. For the most current information on the treatment of trailing blanks, refer to the documentation for the specific database server. - The ANSI standard treats an empty string as a zero length varchar value. ##  Note The software treats an empty string differently, depending on the source type. In a single transaction, the software can push down expressions so that they are performed by the underlying database manager. However, when the software evaluates an expression which includes operands of more than one data type, the software attempts to convert the operands to the same data type first. (Except for national character-set data types which can be pushed down while others in an expression are not. For more information about supported national character-set data types, see varchar [page 480]). When a conversion is required, the software provides a message at validation. If the conversion is illegal, the software provides an error and you must remove the mismatch before executing the job. If the conversion is legal, the software provides a warning indicating that it will not interrupt job execution. ##  Note When the software converts a data type to evaluate an expression, the results might not be what you expect. To avoid legal but incorrect conversions, always validate before executing and examine the circumstance of any data type conversion warnings. ## 3.14.3.3 Conversion among number data types Information Steward uses a type-promotion algorithm to evaluate expressions that contain more than one number data type. Number data types are ranked from highest to lowest, as follows: - decimal - double - real - int If the software encounters expressions that have more than one number data type among the operands, it converts all of the operands to the data type of the operand with the highest ranking type. For example, if A is an int and B is a double, the expression A+B is evaluated by first converting A to double and then adding the two double values. The result is type double. If in addition to A and B, you multiply the result by a decimal number C, then (A+B)*C is evaluated by first converting (A+B) to decimal, and then performing the indicated operations on the two decimal values. The result is type decimal. For addition, subtraction, and multiplication, the operation result will be equal to the higher of the two operands. Content types add an additional dimension to your data by providing meaning. When the data is meaningful, you can better understand and improve the data by creating business rules. Information Steward has predefined content types that include name, firm, phone, date, address, and so on. You can also define your own content types to better define the data unique to your business. For example, create a content type named Product ID for all columns that contain product IDs. You can run a content type profile on your data to have Information Steward suggest content types. During content type profiling, Information Steward suggests predefined and custom content types to applicable columns. Information Steward suggests the content type using custom logic such as the following: - Distinct values or patterns - Column placement ##  Example First and last name columns are typically next to each other. Similarly, address line and ZIP code data are in close proximity. Personal identity numbers in the United States have a distinct pattern. Content types are useful when you create rules. After you've assigned content types to your data, you can apply the content type dependencies to rules and columns. Applying content types to rules helps Data Insight automatically suggest rules during profiling. Also, when you understand these dependencies, you can better recognize the projects that would be impacted if you change the content type definition for a particular column. ## 3.15.1 Creating custom content types When you have industry-specific data that doesn't match any of the pre-defined content types, create a custom content type. To create a custom content type: 1. Choose Manage Content Types . 2. From the Content Types window, click New . 3. Enter a unique name. 4. Enter a description. 5. Click Save . When you assign a custom content type to the data in one project, you might see that content type suggested when you run content type profiling on another table with similar data. ##  Tip Before assigning a custom content type to a column, run a column profiling task with the Median & Distribution option selected. Then training data is associated with the content type and can be suggested for future content type profiling. ## Related Information Creating a column profile task [page 83] ## 3.15.2 Viewing content type dependencies You can view all of the rules and columns that are associated with a content type. Enterprise systems include business intelligence and relational database systems, data warehouse, data integration technologies, and data modeling tools. Metadata provides information about how data is managed within an enterprise system. Metadata includes the following information: - Object attributes such as field name, size, and data type. - Structures such as field and column lengths. - Properties such as data location, associations, and ownership. - Descriptive information about the data context, quality, condition, or characters. Information Steward collects and organizes metadata from enterprise systems, which your or your administrator defines in the Central Management Console as integrator source systems . You can use the integrators to access metadata from the source systems and load it into your Information Steward repository. The work flow below describes the process involved in creating a person and firm cleansing package. 1. Discuss with the SAP Data Services tester the standardization options you need to have set in the Data Cleanse transform so that your cleansed data meets your business rules. 2. Consider some common changes to variations to process data better. 3. Consider some common changes to rules. As you make changes to rules, it may be helpful to view the rule history. 4. If it is needed, create a pattern classification or user-defined classification. Pattern classifications allow you to define an ICU regular expression which matches the acceptable range of a data pattern, such as a part number. When the pattern classification is used in a parsing rule, Data Cleanse looks for parsed values that match the pattern defined in the pattern classification. Cultural standards vary and some cultures require special classifications to achieve accurate parsing results. For example, in Russian a person's middle name is a form of his father's name. In Japanese, there are special indicators for a woman's maiden family name and for a married couple. SAP-supplied cleansing packages already contain special classifications and modified parsing rules to account for these cultural standards. However, you can create a user-defined classification and modify the parsing rules when your unique data requires special treatment. 5. If it is needed, set customization options for common types of data such as email addresses, telephone numbers, dates, and U.S. Social Security numbers. 6. Test your person and firm cleansing package using the Validate tab in Cleansing Package Builder (Advanced mode). The significance of the values is defined by the context in which they are found. For example, in pharmaceutical industry data the value "10 MG PER 1 G" likely refers to a medication dosage. When taken individually each value: 10, MG, PER, 1, or G is not meaningful. However when taken together in context, 10 MG PER 1 G, the values provide useful information and could be assigned to a DOSAGE attribute. Other examples of context include: - part numbers such as HNH457, which can be defined by three letters followed by a range of three digits. - catalog numbers - measurements such as 5 mm or 45 cm that contain a range of values followed by a unit - currency amounts such as $100,000 or €3.50 - any other patterns that contain a defined combination of letters, numbers, and special characters A value may be associated with more than one attribute if it can be used in more than one context. For example, the variation M may mean medium when associated with a size attribute or the variation M may mean meter used as a unit of measure in a measurement context, such as 7 M, and associated with a length attribute. The way the context is defined allows Cleansing Package Builder to differentiate and correctly assign your data. The individual pieces that make up a context definition are called components. For example, the context definition for the measurement 5 mm contains two components: a range of values and a unit of measurement. Components may be optional or repeated within a context. Use Define Context to define a single context that covers the range of data you expect and then define how you want the cleansed data formatted. 6.6.8 Parsed values assigned to more than one attribute (conflict resolution) Sometimes a parsed value may have more than one meaning. For example, M may be taken to mean either medium or meter; cream may be a color, a dairy product, or the formulation of a pharmaceutical or cosmetic product. In these cases, depending on usage, you may want to assign a parsed value to more than one attribute. Often you can accomplish that by defining the context in which the parsed value would occur. For example, if M is preceded by a number, then it means meter. Cleansing Package Builder can assign parsed values to more than one attribute as long as context has been defined for all but one alternative; if your data contains two alternatives, you must define context for at least one of them, if your data contains three alternatives, you must define context for at least two of them and so on. A conflict occurs when you have assigned a parsed value to one attribute and then attempt to assign the same parsed value to a second attribute. You can resolve a conflict in one of several ways: - Define a context. - Specify an adjacent attribute that consistently precedes the attribute to which you want to assign the conflicting parsed value. - Specify an adjacent attribute that consistently follows the attribute to which you want to assign the conflicting parsed value. In effect, when a conflict occurs, specifying an adjacent attribute creates an if-then statement. If the adjacent attribute precedes, then the if-then statement says: IF attribute A precedes, THEN assign the parsed value to attribute B. If the adjacent attribute follows, then the if-then statement says: IF attribute A follows, THEN assign the parsed value to attribute B. To specify a logical and , create a single resolution condition that contains both the attribute that precedes and the attribute that follows the attribute to which you want to assign the conflicting parsed value. To specify a logical or , create two separate resolution conditions; one resolution condition for the attribute that precedes the attribute to which you want to assign the parsed value and a second resolution condition for the attribute that follows the attribute to which you want to assign the parsed value. ##  Note Conflict resolutions are not specific to each parsed value. After you define a resolution condition for the first instance of a specific type of conflict, you can ignore any additional conflict prompts that apply to that same type of conflict. In other words, after defining conflict resolution conditions for the color RED, when you assign the next color, BLACK, the Resolve Conflict dialog opens. You can choose to ignore the conflict and Cleansing Package Builder will apply the existing resolution conditions to BLACK. ## Example For example, automobile data may include both exterior color and interior color. In this case, red would be assigned as an exterior color if preceded by a value such as matte, metallic, or pearl which is assigned to EXT\_FINISH. The data also shows that cloth or leather comes either before red or after red, but never both before and after in the same record. You can describe two resolution conditions to account for this. One that specifies the attribute INT\_COLOR is preceded by the attribute INT\_MATERIAL and a second resolution condition that specifies the attribute INT\_COLOR is followed by the attribute INT\_MATERIAL. For variations that you add, unless a standard form is specified, Data Cleanse will standardize the variation as mixed case (the first letter as upper case and the remaining letters as lower case). Other capitalization options such as all lower case or all upper case can be set in the Data Cleanse transform by a Data Services tester or administrator. ## Editing existing variations To change how a variation is parsed by changing the classification, standard form, attribute, or gender, you must begin by searching for the variation in the Manage tab. Next, select the variation and click Edit . By searching first, you are assured that you have identified the correct variation and are not making unintended changes to a similar variation. ## Adding multiple variations To add new variations, begin in the Manage tab and click Add Variation (+). In the Manage Variations - Add Variation window, click Add Variation (+). Enter the variation name, press Enter . You can keep adding variations to the Manage Variations - Add Variation window, but all variations you add before clicking OK must be assigned identically. In other words, the classification, gender, attribute, standard form, and alternates must be exactly the same for all variations added in one operation. ##  Caution When adding multiple variations at once, if you assign a property (standard form, gender, and so on) to a single variation, all the variations in the group will take on that property. For example, if you need to add several family names, several strong female given names, and several strong male given names you would need to add each group separately. ## Variations in custom cleansing packages For custom cleansing packages, a variation that you add in Advanced mode is also displayed in Design mode as long as the variation is included in your sample data and thus is a parsed value within your sample records. If the variation is not included in your sample data, it will not appear in Design mode in All Records . However, Data Cleanse will recognize and parse the variation if it is included in data used in a Data Cleanse job. ## Phrases and the PHRASE\_WORD classification Your data may contain adjacent values that have meaning

in custom cleansing packages For custom cleansing packages, a variation that you add in Advanced mode is also displayed in Design mode as long as the variation is included in your sample data and thus is a parsed value within your sample records. If the variation is not included in your sample data, it will not appear in Design mode in All Records . However, Data Cleanse will recognize and parse the variation if it is included in data used in a Data Cleanse job. ## Phrases and the PHRASE\_WORD classification Your data may contain adjacent values that have meaning when used together, for example Light blue. Adjacent values used together are referred to as a phrase. In Advanced mode, to create a phrase, you must classify each underlying value as a PHRASE\_WORD and classify the entire phrase appropriately. For example, you would assign the classification PHRASE\_WORD to the variations LIGHT and BLUE, and assign the classification COLOR to Light blue. Person and firm cleansing packages include parsing rules that catch most phrases. In custom cleansing packages, when phrases are created in Design mode, Cleansing Package Builder automatically creates the necessary parsing rules. However when phrases are added manually in Advanced mode, you must ensure that the appropriate parsing rules already exist or write new rules as necessary. ## Related Information Data Cleanse transform options [page 908] Parse and classify input for person and firm cleansing packages [page 889] Parse and classify input for custom cleansing packages [page 892] ## 6.7.3.1 Adding multiple new variations which are assigned identically You can add multiple variations without saving each one individually as long as all the new variations are assigned identically. If you have a pattern in your data such as a part number, you can define a pattern classification containing an ICU regular expression which matches the acceptable range of data. When the pattern classification is used in a parsing rule, Data Cleanse looks for parsed values that match the pattern defined in the pattern classification. Unlike auto-generated or user-defined classifications, you cannot assign parsed values directly to a pattern classification. After you have included a pattern classification in a parsing rule and republished the cleansing package, any data that matches the pattern will be included in the results of a Data Cleanse job. Classifications are not visible in Design mode. ##  Note Pattern classifications and user-defined pattern rules both use ICU regular expressions to customize how Data Cleanse parses your data. For pattern classifications, Data Cleanse searches for individual parsed values that match the regular expression defined in your pattern classification. For user-defined pattern rules, Data Cleanse searches the entire input field specified in the rule for data that matches the regular expression. ## Part number example If your data contains part numbers, you could individually classify each variation as a part number with a userdefined classification of PART\_NUMBER. Alternatively, if you have a large range of acceptable values, it would be more efficient to capture the same data by using an ICU regular expression to define the pattern followed by your part numbers. For this example, we will use TEST as the name of the category and assume that it already exists. To define a pattern classification, attribute and example parsing rule for part numbers: 1. Write an ICU regular expression that captures your part number data. For example, if your part numbers all are a single upper-case letter followed by three numbers, the regular expression would be [A-Z][0-9] {3} . 2. In Advanced mode, click the Manage tab. 3. Click Manage Classifications . 4. Select a pattern and click Add . The Add Pattern Classification window opens. 5. In the Classification Name field, type a name for your classification. For example, type PART\_NUMBER . 6. In the Regular Expression field, type the regular expression that describes the range of acceptable values for part number. For example, type [A-Z][0-9]{3} . 7. (Optional) Enter examples that match the regular expression and click Validate and Test . 8. The portion of the example that matches the regular expression is displayed in Test Results . 8. A single input string can match more than one parsing rule. In the event that more than one parsing rule matches the input string, the rule with the higher confidence score is applied. In the event that more than one parsing rule matches the input string and the rules have equal confidence scores, Data Cleanse applies the first parsing rule in the rule order. You can affect which rule Data Cleanse applies in the following ways: - Add a confidence booster to the confidence score - Move the position of the rule up or down in the rule order (applies only to user-generated rules) ## Confidence booster You can add a weight or confidence booster to the calculated confidence score in order to give a specific rule more or less weight compared to other similar rules. The booster may be a positive or negative integer. If you choose to include a confidence booster, it must be placed in the option line at the beginning of the Rule Action list, immediately following the output type and optional dual name indicator. The following examples of option lines show how user-defined weight can be added to the calculated confidence score. ``` action = PAPER conf : 3; action = PERSON conf : 3; action = PERSON conf : -5; action = PERSON : D conf : 22; ``` ## Scoring and computing confidence in person and firm cleansing packages For each rule that applies to an input string in the PERSON or FIRM categories, Data Cleanse calculates a confidence score. The terms PERSON parse and FIRM parse refer to the specific parser and sequential series of parsed and classified values in an input string. For PERSON rules, Data Cleanse uses a combination of two different, individual scores-the distance score and the look-up score. The distance score is calculated by using weights assigned to each of the parsed components. In contrast, the look-up score is calculated based on how different the parsed value in the input string is from the actual component value. Data Cleanse calculates the difference between these two scores and normalizes the result

Cleanse calculates a confidence score. The terms PERSON parse and FIRM parse refer to the specific parser and sequential series of parsed and classified values in an input string. For PERSON rules, Data Cleanse uses a combination of two different, individual scores-the distance score and the look-up score. The distance score is calculated by using weights assigned to each of the parsed components. In contrast, the look-up score is calculated based on how different the parsed value in the input string is from the actual component value. Data Cleanse calculates the difference between these two scores and normalizes the result to a 100 point scale. For FIRM rules, Data Cleanse compares the number of values classified as FIRM words with the total number of parsed values in the input string, and normalizes the result to a 100 point scale. It then applies adjustments to the score when applicable: - If a FIRM parse contains a FIRM\_TERMINATOR parsed value, 50 points are added to the confidence score. - If a FIRM parse does not use all available parsed values in the input string, the confidence score is halved. - If the resulting confidence score is less than 20, the confidence score is reset to 20, the minimum allowable FIRM confidence score. - If the resulting confidence score is greater than 100, the confidence score is reset to 100, the maximum allowable FIRM confidence score. After Data Cleanse has calculated the internal confidence score for each rule, it applies any additional confidence boosters that are specified in the parsing rules. ## Ranking matching rules in person and firm cleansing packages After Data Cleanse has identified all matching rules and calculated final confidence scores, the rules are then ranked in descending order. If the input string matches only PERSON rules and there is more than one PERSON rule with the same confidence score, Data Cleanse uses the rule that comes first in the rule order. Likewise, If the input string matches only FIRM rules and there is more than one FIRM rule with the same confidence score, Data Cleanse uses the rule that comes first in the rule order. PERSON and FIRM confidence scores are not directly comparable. If the input string matches both PERSON and FIRM rules, Data Cleanse determines which rule to use by using special tie-breaking criteria in the following order: 1. If the PERSON parse contains a TITLE or is a dual name parse containing a PRENAME and none of the FIRM's parsed values are classified as FIRM\_INITIATOR or FIRM\_TERMINATOR, and the FIRM confidence score is not more than 40 greater than the PERSON confidence score, the PERSON parse is used. 2. If the FIRM confidence score is less than 100, the PERSON parse has no FIRM parsed values, the FIRM parse has no CONNECTOR parsed values, and there are no unused FIRM parsed values in the PERSON parse, the PERSON parse is used. 3. If the FIRM confidence score is greater than 50, the FIRM parse is used.

The cleansed data is sent to output fields specified by the Data Services administrator or tester. The Data Cleanse transform follows a multi-step process: - Breaks apart your input data into parsed values and classifies them. - Finds which parsing rule or rules match each field in your data. - Applies the parsing rule which has the highest confidence score. - Outputs your cleansed data. ## Input data formats The uncleansed input data can be in one of the following input field formats: - Discrete - Multiline - Hybrid In a discrete input field format the data is already its most distinct level. For example, a field containing only given names would be discrete, whereas a field containing a mixture of given name, middle name, and family name information would not be discrete, but rather multiline. For example, a field containing only given names would be discrete, whereas a field containing a mixture of given name, middle name, and family name information would not be discrete, but rather multiline. In a multiline input field format the data is not consistently located in the same arrangement for all records. For example, a person and firm multiline input field might contain a person's name in one record and a firm's name in another record. After the input string has been broken into individual parsed values, Data Cleanse attempts to recombine contiguous parsed values-those values that are not separated by white space. Data Cleanse starts with the first parsed value in the input string and attempts to combine it with the next value in the string. The current parsed value is only eligible to be combined with the next parsed value if it meets the following criteria: - It cannot already be a part of a value that is being combined. - It cannot be in the final position in the input string. Because the last parsed value is an S, Data Cleanse first combines the parsed value and looks up the variation including the apostrophe (MACY'S). If the variation in not found, Data Cleanse looks up the variation without the apostrophe (MACYS). If MACYS is not successful, Data Cleanse automatically keeps the values together (MACY'S) and adds the FIRM\_MISCELLANEOUS classification to the variation. When automated data cleansing processes can't determine duplicate records with enough confidence, you can review them manually. Match Review provides you with the tools to review the match groups manually to determine the following: - Whether the records in a match group are unique - Whether the records in a match group are duplicates - What elements of all duplicate records make the best record Information Steward accesses a table from a staging database generated by SAP Data Services. The table contains match groups, which are groups of records that are possible duplicates. Review the possible duplicates in each match group to determine if the records are for the same entity, such as a person or business. If best record creation is enabled, merge the best information from the duplicate records into a single best record. Data Services uses the best record as a reference record for all the downstream processes. ##  Note Best record formation must be enabled in the match review configuration to be able to create the best record during a match review. ## Data Review configuration file [page 946] ## Key steps to incorporate Match Review into data quality processes [page 947] To incorporate a manual match review in SAP Information Steward into your automatic process from SAP Data Services, perform some key steps. ## Coordinate matching between Information Steward and Data Services [page 948] Coordinate match processing between SAP Information Steward and SAP Data Services to reduce the number of match groups for manual review. ## E-Mail notifications for match review tasks [page 972] You can configure SAP Information Steward so that the specified match review administrator, approver, and reviewer receive an e-mail notification for specific match review tasks. ## Match Review Summary dashboard [page 974] When you open a match review task, the Match Review Summary dashboard opens showing a series of tiles that contain statistics about the match groups. ## Implicit master record assignment [page 997] If a match group doesn't have a master record, SAP Information Steward assigns the master record based on the situation. ## Best record lineage table [page 998] The best record lineage table shows where the fields of the best record came from. ## Approving match groups [page 1001] The approver approves or rejects the reviewers' actions. ## Monitoring match review [page 1002] You or someone who belongs to the Data Review Configuration Manager group monitor the overall progress of match reviews to ensure that there are enough reviewers and approvers to complete tasks on time. ## Match review

When a manual review of match groups is necessary, use SAP Data Services to implement the overall matching and consolidation process and to stage the match groups for manual review in SAP Information Steward. ## Considerations To coordinate the match process between Information Steward and Data Services, consider the following factors: ## Create a staging file: - Staging file contains suspect match groups that don't meet your set match score or threshold for manual review. - Staging file contains all match results, including unique records. Data Stewards manually separates suspect records from unique records. The target groups are suspect group and high confidence group. ## Best records: - Enable best record creation in Information Steward. - Data steward manually reviews suspect match groups and Data Services creates the best records after the manual review. If Information Steward creates best records, consider the following issues for creating best records out of the high confidence match groups: - Manually creating a best record for all match groups in a large data set isn't practical. - If you've already consolidated high-confidence match groups within Data Services, then you've already modified the original match group to include

records. The target groups are suspect group and high confidence group. ## Best records: - Enable best record creation in Information Steward. - Data steward manually reviews suspect match groups and Data Services creates the best records after the manual review. If Information Steward creates best records, consider the following issues for creating best records out of the high confidence match groups: - Manually creating a best record for all match groups in a large data set isn't practical. - If you've already consolidated high-confidence match groups within Data Services, then you've already modified the original match group to include the best record values. Therefore, you can't stage these modified match groups for manual review in Information Steward. ## Approaches The following examples illustrate possible methods for coordinating a match review between the two products. ##  Example Data Services performs automated matching and splits the output into two target databases: - Suspect match groups - High confidence match groups Route the suspect match groups to Information Steward, where data stewards and domain experts perform a manual review to create best records. Route the high confidence match group database through another match process in Data Services. Configure the Match transform to create best records out of the match groups, and output the best records to the original source database. <!-- image --> ##  Example Data stewards and domain experts perform a manual review and correct of all match groups. However, Data Services performs the best record creation and consolidation. To coordinate a match review in this manner, perform the following steps: 1. Process the data in Data Services with automated matching. Data Services outputs all match results to a staging database. The database contains the following groups: - Suspect match groups - High confidence match groups - Unique records 2. Send the output from Data Services to Information Steward. Data stewards and domain experts can manually review and correct the suspect match groups. The reviewers can move the records between suspect match groups and high confidence match groups, or include a unique record in the appropriate match group. 3. The resulting database goes back to Data Services to be processed with a new match job that creates the best record and consolidates all match groups. Configure the Match transform to create best records out of already-matched groups of records. ##  Note For examples of best record creation using Information Steward or Data Services, download the Data Quality Management Match blueprints and accompanying user guide from https:/ /wiki.scn.sap.com/wiki/ display/EIM/SAP+Data+Services+Blueprints ## 8.4 Match review configuration ## 8.4.1 Creating a match review configuration A match review configuration controls the match review process, which includes initiating match review tasks. SAP Information Steward combines the best values for the specified columns to create one true version of the records in the match group. All downstream processes, such as processes in SAP Data Services, use the best record. Create a best record strategy in step 3 of the match review configuration wizard. Create a best record strategy only when the process isn't performed by SAP Data Services or another application that creates the match staging file. You must define at least two best record strategies for each display column, except when the first strategy is Aggregate, Concatenation, or Apply Fixed Value. When the first strategy is Aggregate, Concatenation, or Apply Fixed Value, you can't set strategies for the 1st and 2nd tie breaker strategies. Define a strategy for 2nd Tie Breaker Strategy only when the strategy for 1st Tie Breaker Strategy could still result in duplicate records. When you review match groups, Information Steward applies the best record strategies. If your configuration contains three best record strategies per column, Information Steward determines the best value for the column as follows: - Information Steward applies the Main Strategy first. Run a match review configuration immediately from the Match Review Configurations dialog box in SAP Information Steward. Or, open the Central Management Console (CMC) and run a match review configuration immediately or set it to run on a schedule. In the CMC, Find the match review configuration in the Match Review node of the Information Steward page. Set a schedule for regular execution based on factors, such as how often SAP Data Services runs the automated matching job. For scheduled match review configurations, the match review Job Service runs a match review configuration only when: - The input table contains new match groups. - The job status table indicates that the match results are ready for review. When a match review configuration is ready to run, the match review Job Service performs the following tasks: - Creates a new match review task, which contains all new match groups with the same job instance ID - Inserts the task in the worklist of the assigned reviewer and, if required, approver - Sends an e-mail alert to the listed reviewer in the My Worklist tab. Applicable only when e-mail alerts are configured for the reviewer. All tasks generated from the same match review configuration have the same reviewer and approver. However, if necessary, you can edit the task to change the reviewers and approvers for a task. However, in some cases a record can end up in an incorrect match group. For example, Data Services identifies a record as unique when it really is a duplicate that belongs in a match group. To resolve these differences, you move records in or out of a match group. SAP Information Steward enables you to move records during a match review in the following ways: - Move one or more records out of the match group into other groups. - Move one or more records from other groups into the match group - Move unique records out of the match group - Merge two match groups by moving the master record from one group to another group. - Create a new match group with two or more records from the Match Group List. ## Match group status You can move records into and out of the match group when the status of the group you're reviewing is For Review or Rejected . If the group that you're reviewing doesn't have the applicable status, modify the group to change the status to For Review . ##  Note For instructions to modify a match group, see Modifying a match group [page 996]. Group statuses change when you move records from group to group. A group into which you move a record is a target group. After you move a record from the review match group to a target group, the status of the target group changes from Reviewed , Approved , or Auto Confirmed to For Review . T arget groups with a status of Rejected retain the rejected status. You can't move records out of or into

change the status to For Review . ##  Note For instructions to modify a match group, see Modifying a match group [page 996]. Group statuses change when you move records from group to group. A group into which you move a record is a target group. After you move a record from the review match group to a target group, the status of the target group changes from Reviewed , Approved , or Auto Confirmed to For Review . T arget groups with a status of Rejected retain the rejected status. You can't move records out of or into match groups with the status of Completed . Information Steward assigns a group the Completed status based on a setting in the match review configuration. During configuration, your administrator selects one of the following options to determine when a match group's status changes to Completed : - When the match group has been reviewed, and if necessary, approved - When the match review task is completed ## Match history Moving records from one match group to another can get confusing. This information makes it easier for you to verify the move after it is complete. Information Steward assigns a name to the best record lineage table using the following naming conventions: <!-- formula-not-decoded --> A data steward can refer to the best record lineage table when the best record seems incorrect, and before changing the best record. Information in the best record lineage table answers the following questions: - Where did the best record column values come from? - Which sources contributed to the best record? - Were any column values manually entered ## Contents of the best record lineage table The best record lineage table contains information in the following columns: - Job\_ID - Group\_Number - Source\_System - Source\_Record\_ID - All column names in the source records To indicate whether Information Steward used the source value or the value was manually entered or altered, the best record lineage table contains values as described in the following table. | Column value | Description | |----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | Null | Indicates that the column didn't contribute to the best re­ cord value.  Note For the Source_System and Source_Record_ID columns, in which nulls aren't allowed, the values are as follows: ● '_' (underscore) when the columns contain string data types ● -1 when the columns contain numeric data types | | 1 | Indicates that the column contributed to the best record value. | Additionally, the best record lineage table contains the following: - A row for each match record from which the best record values came - A row for best record values that were entered manually ## Examples ##  Example You reviewed a match group named Customer. Make to stock 2. Make to order 3. Engineer to order The manufacturing method depends on the type of products that your company manufactures. But first, let's take a look at each of these to understand what they are. ## 1.1 Make to stock Make to stock is a method in which products are mass-produced and stored in warehouses. This is the most common type of manufacturing method where the produced stock is either sent out to distributors or sold to customers (other businesses). For example, fast moving consumer goods (FMCG) products, clothes, furniture, etc. A standard bill of materials (BOM) is used as a recipe to manufacture items and maintain the stock levels. Hence the term make to <!-- image --> <!-- image --> stock. The stock to be manufactured in advance is generally projected based on demand forecasting. ## 1.2 Make to Order In this method, items are manufactured only when the company receives an order. This is often done in high value or specialized items where there is no large consumer market and selling them takes a long time. For example, specialized machinery equipment or parts but the BOM remains the same for every product. Since the manufacturing happens only when a sales order is received, hence it's called make to order. ## 1.3 Engineer to Order This goes one step further where the item is produced based on custom requirements specified by the buyer, which means that each product is unique. Usually, these items are not mass-produced, for example, furniture with custom dimensions or materials. For each order, the specifications are different and a different BOM is created, hence engineer to order. ## 2. Common challenges Now, you may face multiple challenges in day-to-day manufacturing, we don't understand them 100% and won't pretend to. Pilferage or misplaced goods during transit, lack of systems to verify these. Poor efficiency causes things like delayed deliveries to customers. ## 2.2 Lack of software systems For a manufacturing business, be it SMB or an enterprise, the need for a complete ERP solution is inevitable. According to Wikipedia, Odoo is an all-in-one management software that offers a range of business applications that form a complete suite of enterprise management applications. The Odoo solution is ideal for SMEs, but fits both small and large companies alike. Odoo is an all-in-one business software capable of covering all business needs, including CRM, website/e-commerce, billing, accounting, manufacturing, warehouse, project management, and inventory, all seamlessly integrated. Tips: In 2005, Fabien Pinckaers, the Founder and CEO of Odoo, started to develop his first software product, TinyERP. Later in the beginning of 2009 it was renamed to OpenERP, in May 2014, the company was renamed Odoo, a name that has no restrictions and can allow the company to grow in whichever direction. Odoo offers two different versions of the solution; Odoo Enterprise and Odoo Community Edition. The community edition is free to download and can be used anywhere. The Enterprise edition comes with many out of the box applications, unlimited support software support, migration service. The Enterprise edition can be available as Odoo Online SaaS (Software as a Service) or on Odoo.sh or you can install on your private server too. The Odoo Online version is hosted on a cloud, and the first app is offered for free for unlimited users. After the first app, there is a fixed monthly subscription fee for the number of apps installed and the number of users. The Community version is the open source version and available for free to use on your own server. Today, more and more companies are choosing to host their business application on an Odoo online cloud platform, it is too costly for the companies to host their business application on local hardware. This approach requires not only a lot of capital to buy hardware and software licenses, but also creates a lot of responsibilities and risk in backing up data and ensuring stability of the business application. Try Odoo now, and join 2 millions of happy users. ## KAPITEL 5 ## Accounting and Finance ## 5.2 The Accounting behind Odoo This page summarises the way Odoo deals with typical accounts and transactions. ## 5.2.1 Double-entry bookkeeping Odoo automatically creates all the behind-the-scenes journal entries for each of your accounting transactions: customer invoices, point of sale order, expenses, inventory moves, etc. Odoo uses the rules of double-entry bookkeeping system: all journal entries are automatically balanced (sum of debits = sum of credits). ## 5.2.2 Accrual and Cash Basis Methods Odoo support both accrual and cash basis reporting. This allows you to report income / expense at the time transactions occur (i.e., accrual basis), or when payment is made or received (i.e., cash basis). ## 5.2.3 Multi-companies Odoo allows to manage several companies within the same database. Each company has its own chart of accounts and rules. You can get consolidation reports following your consolidation rules. Users can access several companies but always work in one company at a time. ## 5.2.4 Multi-currencies Every transaction is recorded in the default currency of the company. For transactions occurring in another currency, Odoo stores both the value in the currency of the company and the value in the currency of the transaction. Odoo can generate currencies gains and losses after the reconciliation of the journal items. Odoo's reports range from basic accounting reports to advanced management reports. Odoo's reports include: - Performance reports (such as Profit and Loss, Budget Variance) - Position reports (such as Balance Sheet, Aged Payables, Aged Receivables) - Cash reports (such as Bank Summary) - Detail reports (such as Trial Balance and General Ledger) - Management reports (such as Budgets, Executive Summary) - Odoo's report engine allows you to customize your own report based on your own formulae. ## 5.2.8 Import bank feeds automatically Bank reconciliation is a process that matches your bank statement lines, as supplied by the bank, to your accounting transactions in the general ledger. Odoo makes bank reconciliation easy by frequently importing bank statement lines from your bank directly into your Odoo account. This means you can have a daily view of your cashflow without having to log into your online banking or wait for your paper bank statements. Odoo speeds up bank reconciliation by matching most of your imported bank statement lines to your accounting transactions. Odoo also remembers how you've treated other bank statement lines and provides suggested general ledger transactions. ## 5.2.9 Calculates the tax you owe your tax authority Odoo totals all your accounting transactions for your tax period and uses these totals to calculate your tax obligation. This guide provides an overview ERP system implementation best practices and strategies. Key Benefits of ERP Systems: 1. Improved Data Visibility - ERP systems provide a single source of truth for all business d enabling better decision-making across departments and functions. 2. Enhanced Operational Efficiency - By automating routine tasks and streamlining processes E systems reduce manual work and improve overall productivity across the organization. 3. Better Financial Management - ERP systems provide real-time financial reporting and foreca capabilities helping organizations manage cash flow and profitability. 4. Improved Customer Service - With integrated customer data organizations can provide better service and support to their customers. Implementation Phases: Phase 1: Planning and Assessment - Evaluate current business processes and identify areas for improvement and optimization in the organization. Phase 2: System Selection - Choose an ERP solution that meets organizational needs and budget constraints effectively. Phase 3: Configuration and Customization - Configure the ERP system to match existing busines processes and requirements. Phase 4: Data Migration - Transfer existing data from legacy systems to the new ERP system carefully. All rights reserved. -  Now let us take a look at the procurement process and its effect on inventory and accounting. -  When a purchase order is created, there are no postings in inventory and accounting. -  The first posting will be made when a goods receipt PO is entered. The GRPO creates a journal entry that posts the value of the received goods to the debit side of the stock account and to the credit side of an allocation cost account. -  The stock account and the allocation cost account are retrieved from the Inventory Account field and the Allocation Account field on the Inventory Data tab of the item master record. -  The allocation cost account is a transfer account used to check if goods receipt POs and the A/P invoices match. -  The allocation account's total balance represents the value of all open goods receipts POs that are not yet copied to an A/P invoice. -  Later, when the A/P invoice is posted, the goods receipt PO is closed. -  At that point, the A/P invoice creates a journal entry that posts the invoiced amount to the debit side of the allocation costs account and to the credit side of the vendor account. -  In this way, the amount in the Allocation Cost account from the goods receipt PO is cleared and the system records the amount owed to the vendor. ## Streamlined Procurement Process <!-- image --> 2013 SAP AG. So you call the vendor and ask them to deliver the item today. Because of the hurry, you skip the purchase order. -  When the item is delivered, the vendor invoice is also delivered. -  So rather than creating a goods receipt PO, you enter an A/P invoice to process both the receipt of the items into inventory and the obligation to pay the vendor. -  In this case, when you directly post the A/P invoice without first creating a goods receipt PO, the postings to the allocation costs account are omitted. The posting debits the stock account to show the increase in inventory and credits the vendor account to show the need to pay the vendor. -  Because an A/P invoice that does not reference a goods receipt PO will increase inventory, it is important to make sure there is no prior goods receipt if you create an A/P invoice without reference. ## Summary <!-- image --> Here are some points to take away: key - The four basic steps of the procurement process are: the purchase order; the goods receipt PO, the A/P invoice and the outgoing payment. - Two key types of master data in purchasing are vendor master data and item master data. - In a streamlined purchasing process; the only mandatory document is the A/P invoice. - The A/P invoice is designed to increase inventory when the invoice does not reference a goods receipt PO as a base document. 2013 SAP AG.
